name: Seve Ballesteros-Santander Airport
before:
Cantabria's only airport, just outside Santander. It handled 1,103,353 passengers in 2018, a long way up from 180,000 in 1995, though traffic has slipped back since in line with the wider Spanish pattern.

It is a small and simple building: eight check in desks, three baggage carousels and seven boarding gates, with the ability to handle flights from outside the Schengen zone.

The runway has an unusual setting. It is 2,420 metres, built on ground reclaimed from the Bay of Santander, and runway 29 finishes about 20 metres from the water while runway 11 ends 150 metres from the S-10 highway and a shopping centre. A precision approach lighting system was added at runway 29 in 2021.

Buses run from Santander's main bus station in the centre, and ALSA coaches on the routes to Bilbao, Gijón, Oviedo and Laredo will stop at the airport if booked in advance.

The airport opened in 1977 and was renamed in April 2015 after Seve Ballesteros, the golfer, who was born at Pedreña a few kilometres away.
after:
Santander's airport, at Maliaño just outside the city. It handled just over a million passengers in 2025, about 2 per cent fewer than in 2024.

The terminal is small and simple, and it can handle flights from outside the Schengen area.

Its single runway, 2,320 metres long, sits on reclaimed marshland beside the Bay of Santander.

Buses run between the airport and Santander's bus station, and ALSA coaches on the routes to Bilbao, Gijón, Oviedo and Laredo will stop at the airport if booked in advance.

The airport first opened in 1953 and was largely rebuilt between 1973 and 1977. It was renamed in April 2015 after the golfer Seve Ballesteros, who was born nearby at Pedreña.
